observations.attribution: IBBS among injecting drug users in Podgorica, based on Respondent Driven Sampling (RDS) methodology.
observations.caveat:
In accordance with the recommendations of the Protocol on the implementation of bio-behavioral studies among at-risk populations in Montenegro, only an estimate of the size of the population of people who inject drugs was made. An estimate of the size of the population of people who inject drugs has been made is using the multiplier method and the "Successive sampling population size estimation" (SS-PSE) technique.
The most recent estimate of PWID (last month injecting) was obtained in 2020 by means of service multiplier and successive sampling population size estimation (SS PSE) methods, within the RDS survey of seroprevalence of HIV, hepatitis B and C among PWID. By the service multiplier method, it was estimated that there are 1120 [CI 95% 691-1550] PWID in the capital Podgorica. The rate per 1000 inhabitants is 8.5 . Data for the service multiplier (number of PWIDs who used NSE and condom distribution programmes in the specified period) was obtained from services for PWID - drop-in centers and outreach agencies. It is possible that the actual numbers are higher, since the COVID-19 pandemic in the country led to curfew and reduced mobility and service utilization at the time of the survey.
SS_PSE method estimated 1248 [CI 95% 901-2597] PWID in the capital. The rate per 1000 inhabitants is 9.5. Males largely prevail in the population of PWID in Podgorica, whose proportion is estimated at 88.3%, while the estimated proportion of females is 11.7%. This data is compared with the programme data from the PWID services (drop in centres) where proportion of female users is 12.9%.

observations.attribution: UNAIDS GAM; Integrated Behavioral Biological Study among PWID in Podgorica: https://www.unaids.org/en/regionscountries/countries/montenegro
IBBS "Survey on HIV/AIDS risk behavior, HIV, HBV and HCV seroprevalence among injecting drug users in Podgorica, Montenegro in 2020
observations.caveat:
The survey was conducted in the capital Podgorica, where around of 1/3 inhabitants of the country live.
In accordance with the recommendations of the Protocol on the implementation of bio-behavioral studies among at-risk populations in Montenegro, only an estimate of the size of the population of people who inject drugs was made. An estimate of the size of the population of people who inject drugs has been made is using the multiplier method and the "Successive sampling population size estimation" (SS-PSE) technique.
We conducted a cross-sectional bio-behavioral survey among PWID in Podgorica using respondent-driven sampling (RDS) in people who use drugs (PWID) in Podgorica (a single-sample study) Montenegro in 2020 in order to determine the prevalence of HIV, hepatitis C (HCV), hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and risk behaviors.  Recruitment was initiated with four seeds (initial participants). Seeds were diverse in respect to age and a place of residence in the city. Seeds, as well as each participant who completed the survey, were provided with three coupons to be used in recruiting maximum of three eligible participants. Eligible participants were individuals older than 18 years living in Podgorica for at least 3 months during 12 months before the survey and who injected drugs for non-medical purposes in a month preceding the survey. Before agreeing to participate in the survey, participants were described the nature and characteristics of the survey and were asked for a verbal consent to participate. Following the consent, participants completed a questionnaire and were afterwards provided with pre-test HIV counseling and taken a sample of venous blood. Primary monetary incentive and three coupons for peer recruitment were given to participants after completion of the abovementioned steps of the survey. Participants were instructed to re-visit the survey site in 14 days in order to collect secondary incentives and test results. Post-test counseling was provided after issuing HIV, HCV, and HBsAg test results. A sample of 400 respondents, people who inject drugs, was determined in accordance with the Research Protocol in accordance with the defined criteria. Data were analyzed using RDS Analyst and SPSS 26 to obtain prevalence estimates of key bio-behavioral indicators. 
Blood samples were tested in the laboratory of the Center for Medical Microbiology of the IPH, which serves as a national referral center for HIV testing. Serum samples were tested for the presence of HIV-1/2 antibodies and p24 antigen using ELISA (HIV Ab&Ag, Dia.Pro Diagnostic Bioprobes srl., Milano, Italy). ELISA was also used for detection of antibodies against HCV (HCV Ab, Dia.Pro Diagnostic Bioprobes srl., Milano, Italy) and HBsAg (HBsAgone Version ULTRA, Dia.Pro Diagnostic Bioprobes srl., Milano, Italy).
